newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds hold firm as U.S. Treasuries slip.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds hold firm as U.S. Treasuries slip.

text.p: Emerging market debt fended off a slump in the U.S. bond market on Friday, as strong sentiment in Argentina and optimism about Russia's upcoming Eurobond held up a healthy bid tone, Brady bond traders said.
"The market is stronger overall, outperforming the Treasury bond," one Brady bond trader at a major U.S. bank said. "But not a whole lot is going on."
Traders described activity as sluggish, as portfolio managers made minor adjustments to their positions with the year-end approaching.
"I dont think there were any huge bets, but clients at this point still have a lot of cash that they are looking to put to work," the trader said.
Brazil's financial markets were closed on Friday for the second round of mayoral elections and the absense of players from Sao Paulo made the thin Brady bond market more illiquid.
Argentine players drove their local bond market higher on optimism the country's recovery was proceeding faster than anticipated, traders said.
On Wednesday, Argentina announced that its economy grew 6.6 percent in the third quarter year-over-year.
"There is an optimistic feeling in the market about Argentina," another Brady bond trader said.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1/8 to 84-5/8 bid, while the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond at 1515 EDT/2000 GMT lost 15/32 to yield 6.46 percent.

Russian debt prices gained on continued optimism about the country's Eurobond issue, which is currently being presented to investors at a roadshow. Russian Vnesh dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR gained 1/2 point to 80-5/8.
Brazil kept its luster after the government on Thursday unveiled a whopping $1.308 billion trade deficit for October.
Brazilian debt prices held their own after the data and some dealers said the market survived its worst fears.
Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR rose 1/4 to a bid of 71-1/8, while the country's other Brady bonds were mostly unchanged.

"I think (Brazilian C bonds) will rally because all the bad news about the deficit is pretty much short-term," said Marcelo Fleury, vice president at Garband Corp. "Brazil will attract a lot of foreign direct investment that will more than compensate for the trade deficit."
